title: The Ticketmaster Oasis case shows live-event pricing harm being converted into prospective disclosure and monitoring controls
source_unit: UK Competition and Markets Authority Ticketmaster consumer-protection case concerning Oasis Live '25 ticket sales
geography: United Kingdom; Ticketmaster UK live-event ticket buyers and prospective buyers

denominator.unit: Ticketmaster/Oasis consumers and prospective buyers; case page does not disclose a single affected-customer count

case_opened.unit: date CMA opened investigation into Ticketmaster's Oasis ticket sale

concern_surface.value: dynamic pricing, unclear price information, misleading ticket labels, and purchase pressure during online sales

case_closed.unit: date CMA case was recorded as closed after undertakings

mechanism.value: Scarcity and queue pressure can make price information a decision-control surface: consumers may commit before understanding the final or variable price

observations.method: CMA published case page documenting the opening, concerns, consultation, undertakings, and closure of the consumer-protection investigation.
observations.uncertainty: The case page records regulatory concerns and outcome but does not quantify consumer overpayment, abandoned purchases, attendance loss, or individual financial harm.
observations.subgroup: Consumers attempting to buy Oasis Live '25 tickets through Ticketmaster UK and the investigated firm.
observations.counterinterpretation: Dynamic pricing can reflect genuine scarcity or demand management; the case does not establish that every price change was unlawful or that every buyer was misled.

denominator.unit: Ticketmaster UK sales process; no affected-customer denominator disclosed

advance_notice.unit: advance notice required if a tiered pricing system is used

queue_price_information.value: Ticketmaster must provide more information about ticket prices during online queues

misleading_labels.value: Ticketmaster must not use misleading ticket labels

reporting_duration.unit: years of regular reporting to the CMA

mechanism.value: When individual financial loss is difficult to identify or restore, regulators can target information asymmetry and interface pressure prospectively through conduct undertakings and monitoring

observations.method: CMA case outcome describing undertakings signed by Ticketmaster and the associated reporting obligation.
observations.uncertainty: The undertaking page does not report compliance observations, future price levels, customer comprehension, or whether the controls changed access for lower-income fans.
observations.subgroup: Ticketmaster UK customers and prospective customers exposed to tiered pricing, online queues, and ticket labels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Disclosure may not neutralize scarcity, affordability, or behavioral pressure; consumers can understand a price and still be unable to purchase at it.

observations.period: StubHub versus Ticketmaster comparison; remedy-stage distinction

denominator.unit: Two separate CMA live-event consumer-protection cases; no harmonized affected-consumer denominator

stubhub_remedy.value: automatic refunds exceeding £590,000 to 51,350 customers plus an £889,200 fine
stubhub_remedy.unit: retrospective monetary redress and penalty in the comparator case

ticketmaster_remedy.value: prospective undertakings on notice, queue information, labels, and two-year reporting; no direct refund total stated on the case page

mechanism.value: Consumer protection has at least two distinct conversion paths: recover money after an executable fee violation, or reduce future information asymmetry when harm is prospective and harder to individualize

observations.method: Cross-case comparison of two official CMA live-event enforcement records; the cases are not treated as statistically comparable populations.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison cannot estimate relative harm, remedy effectiveness, deterrence, or consumer welfare because the cases involve different conduct, firms, affected populations, and remedy designs.
observations.subgroup: Consumers purchasing or attempting to purchase live-event tickets in the two CMA cases.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different remedies may reflect legal findings, evidence availability, firm cooperation, or case posture rather than a general hierarchy of consumer-protection effectiveness.

related_sources.claim: The StubHub case provides the retrospective-redress comparator: more than £590,000 in automatic refunds to 51,350 customers and an £889,200 fine.
The CMA's outcome notice describes the Ticketmaster undertakings and the consumer-information changes following the Oasis investigation.

boundary: This record adds a named UK live-event pricing episode and contrasts prospective transparency/reporting controls with retrospective automatic refund remedy. It does not establish unlawful conduct for every dynamic price, quantify consumer losses, verify future compliance, estimate attendance exclusion, or prove that disclosure restores affordability.
